analysis.summary: The experiment successfully demonstrates that Brain-5D can generate stable spike dynamics over 100,000 simulation ticks without numerical drift. All 20 runs (10 no_input_control and 10 tonic_drive) completed without errors, maintaining stable neuron voltages and spike counts.

key_findings.description: All runs completed the required burn-in period of 10,000 ticks without issues.
Minimum neuron voltage remained stable across all runs, indicating no numerical drift.
Consistent spike rate of 300 spikes per tick was maintained throughout the simulation.
Spike counts remained stable across all windows, confirming consistent network activity.
All runs passed the stability check, indicating no significant numerical drift or errors.

analysis.conclusion: The experiment confirms that Brain-5D can generate stable spike dynamics over 100,000 simulation ticks without numerical drift. The tonic_drive condition showed consistent performance with stable neuron voltages and spike counts, meeting the requirements for sustained activity stability.

next_steps: Validate the results with additional runs using different seeds and configurations.
Conduct a detailed analysis of spike timing and interval distribution to assess temporal dynamics.
Explore the impact of varying drive currents on long-term stability.
limitations: No registered scientific evidence is linked to this experiment.
The analysis is based on deterministic statistics and requires semantic validation.
